caption:
What does "glass skin" actually mean in Korean?
Something the English translation dropped on the way out.

English beauty vocabulary describes how skin looks. Korean describes what skin is doing. That sounds like a small difference until you are sitting in a consultation trying to explain a problem.

Mul-gwang is literally water-shine. Not a glossy surface - the look of light sitting just under skin that is holding water. Sok-dang-gim is inner pull: oily on top, tight underneath, which is a common and genuinely confusing state to describe in English. Gyeol is grain, narrower and more exact than "texture". Dong-an is a face that reads young, rather than skin that looks new.

None of these name a look. Each one names a condition.

Which is why it matters in the room. "I want glass skin" describes a result you have seen. "I get tightness underneath even when my face is oily" describes your skin. The second one gets you a better conversation, in any language.

You are not learning Korean. You are learning six nouns.

General education only.

first_comment: The one that has no clean English equivalent is sok-dang-gim - oily on the surface and tight underneath at the same time. Which word were you missing?
